what: development: the memory's proposals with a clock and with a count of fits, on development tables of the small-table reading (scripts/study_counted_memory.py)
machine: the development workspace, two workers side by side on two cores
reading: The memory's growth was stopped by its 5-second clock on 57 of 60 tables, and on 30 the remembered whole laws ran into their 15-second clock as well: what the memory proposes depends on how fast the machine is on nearly every table.
With both clocks halved, as on a machine half as fast, the proposals differed on 23 of 60 tables; the true form was among them on 10 tables against 11 (one gained, two lost).

Counting fits instead (1,500 for the growth, 400 for the remembered whole laws) gave the same proposals twice on all 60 tables. The true form was among them on 10 tables against the timed memory's 11 (none gained, one lost), for about the same time (median 18 s).

Development, on tables the reading was developed on, with two workers side by side on two cores. Not in force; replacing the timed memory is the owner's decision and would be compared on fresh tables first.
